claims.text: The initial alloy is equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
The initial alloy has a nominal single-phase BCC structure.
No major second-phase particles are initially present.
Temperature-dependent thermal-expansion mismatch among the constituent elements creates internal stress fields in HfNbTaTiZr.
Mismatch-generated internal stresses couple to dislocation networks, short-range order, or incipient precipitates.
The coupled internal stresses and evolving microstructure govern stress-strain response, high-temperature creep, elastic moduli, and processing- or aging-dependent hardness.
Local residual-stress concentrations caused by expansion disparities alter dislocation motion.
Local residual-stress concentrations caused by expansion disparities alter potential precipitation sites.
High-temperature mechanical behavior is controlled primarily by dislocation morphology and density.
Mismatch-driven localized stresses reinforce dislocation pile-ups and accelerate or impede dislocation annihilation.
Mismatch-driven localized stresses promote incipient precipitate nucleation during aging at 600–800 °C.
The proposed dislocation and precipitation processes alter yield strength, hardness, creep resistance, and thermoelastic behavior.
In situ diffraction will reveal transient lattice-strain peaks associated with temperature-dependent strengthening or weakening.
The predicted lattice-strain peaks will coincide with changes in dislocation activity, hardness, creep rate, and elastic moduli.
Changing element ratios to reduce thermal-expansion mismatch will reduce internal stresses and suppress mechanical anomalies relative to nominal HfNbTaTiZr.
Below 600 °C or above 1250 °C, diffusion-driven coarsening or oxidation may dominate and diminish the influence of expansion mismatch.
Oxidation, atomic ordering, or other phase transformations may overshadow mismatch effects under some conditions.
Identical internal-strain states and mechanical responses in nominal and mismatch-reduced specimens would falsify expansion mismatch as the governing factor.
